hook: spock had a childhood.
fact: Leonard Nimoy based the Vulcan salute on a Jewish blessing he remembered seeing as a boy.

hook: the guest star had been to space.
fact: Astronaut Mae Jemison appeared in The Next Generation's Second Chances after her real shuttle mission.

hook: uhura opened more than channels.
fact: Nichelle Nichols helped NASA recruit women and minority astronauts for the Space Shuttle program.

hook: the fans named a spaceship.
fact: A fan letter-writing campaign helped get NASA's first space shuttle orbiter named Enterprise.

hook: Kirk was wearing green all along.
fact: Kirk's famous gold command tunic was actually avocado green. Studio lighting and film stock helped turn its color yellow on television.

hook: starfleet checked their references.
fact: NASA astronauts Terry Virts and Mike Fincke made guest appearances in the Enterprise finale.
tag: actual space: already on the resume.

hook: The finale began in six days.
fact: Ronald D. Moore and Brannon Braga wrote the first draft of All Good Things in six days while also working on the film Star Trek Generations.

hook: Picard’s vineyard was in California.
fact: The future vineyard scenes in All Good Things were filmed at a winery in Temecula, California. Picard’s retirement looked French with a little geographical assistance.

hook: Those whales almost had biblical names.
fact: The Voyage Home’s humpbacks George and Gracie were originally called Adam and Evie. The whales changed names while the story developed through its drafts.

hook: The aquarium changed its address.
fact: The Voyage Home filmed at Monterey Bay Aquarium, but the story needed Sausalito. The real institution’s name could not be used for its fictional location.

hook: Even Sarek could be stopped at security.
fact: A cut Voyage Home scene had a guard refuse Sarek entry for lacking credentials. Christine Chapel stepped in to identify the famous Vulcan ambassador.

hook: The tribbles used to be fuzzies.
fact: David Gerrold first submitted The Trouble with Tribbles as The Fuzzies. The furry creatures kept their reproductive enthusiasm while losing their original name.

hook: The writer wrote himself a part.
fact: An early Trouble with Tribbles draft gave Ensign Freeman a job collecting the creatures. David Gerrold had written that small part for himself.

hook: Starfleet still had to collect the mail.
fact: An early Tribbles outline sent the Enterprise to the station partly to collect the crew’s mail. Even a starship’s adventures could include an ordinary postal stop.

hook: The transporter sparkle was aluminum dust.
fact: Original Star Trek’s transporter glitter was filmed aluminum dust falling through strong light. Effects artists combined those particles with the disappearing actors using separate mattes.

hook: Some stars started black on white.
fact: To create the Enterprise’s rushing star field, effects artists painted black stars on a white background, then combined moving layers at different speeds.

hook: Alien clouds came from a liquid tank.
fact: Star Trek’s strange, churning space formations could be dyes fed into clear liquid. Filming those spreading colors made an ordinary tank look unexpectedly cosmic.

hook: A planet could simply be turned over.
fact: Effects artist Joseph Westheimer described reusing Star Trek planets by changing colors, shifting their positions or turning them upside down. New worlds sometimes began with old footage.

hook: The camera did much of the flying.
fact: For many original Enterprise effects, the camera’s movement created most of the apparent travel. The starship could look fast while the model barely went anywhere.

hook: Vulcan dialogue followed English lips.
fact: A Wrath of Khan scene was filmed in English before becoming Vulcan. Marc Okrand invented syllables that matched the actors’ existing lip movements.

hook: A lunch invitation opened the airlock.
fact: Marc Okrand was in Los Angeles for captioning work when lunch with Paramount friends led to a language job. He had not arrived seeking Star Trek work.

hook: Scotty helped invent Klingon.
fact: James Doohan devised the Klingon lines heard in The Motion Picture. Marc Okrand later treated those sounds as the foundation for a much fuller language.

hook: The language expert also captioned the Oscars.
fact: Before teaching aliens to talk, Marc Okrand helped bring live captions to the 1982 Oscars. His television work connected fictional languages with real accessibility.

hook: An actor’s mistake could change the dictionary.
fact: Marc Okrand sometimes adapted Klingon words to actors’ mispronunciations. A later unsalvageable line was made correct through changes included in the revised dictionary.

hook: Scotty used a hand double.
fact: James Doohan lost a finger after being wounded on D-Day. Carefully framed shots and a hand double helped hide the injury when Scotty operated the controls.

hook: Scotty’s accent had a wartime teacher.
fact: James Doohan learned an Aberdeen soldier’s accent during the war. He later softened that brogue for Scotty so television audiences could understand their engineer.

hook: McCoy once directed planes at Roswell.
fact: Before playing the Enterprise’s doctor, DeForest Kelley worked as a military control-tower operator in Roswell, New Mexico. His earlier station already had a famous sci-fi address.

hook: The poker player really was Hawking.
fact: Data’s poker scene paired actors playing Einstein and Newton with the actual Stephen Hawking. The scientist appeared as a holographic version of himself.

hook: Lucy’s studio helped launch the Enterprise.
fact: Lucille Ball’s Desilu backed Star Trek through two pilots after the first failed to win a series order. The sitcom star helped make space for science fiction.

hook: A Talosian also became Cousin Itt.
fact: Felix Silla appeared as a Talosian in The Cage, played Cousin Itt on The Addams Family and later became Twiki in Buck Rogers.

hook: Nimoy invented the quieter knockout.
fact: Leonard Nimoy devised the Vulcan nerve pinch for The Enemy Within. The actor replaced a more conventional scripted knockout with a move that felt more like Spock.

hook: The monster arrived before its story.
fact: According to Star Trek’s production history, Janos Prohaska demonstrated his Horta costume in the office. The strange creature inspired Gene Coon’s Devil in the Dark story.

hook: Hamlet really has a Klingon edition.
fact: The Klingon Language Institute published a complete Klingon Hamlet. A joke about Shakespeare’s original language in The Undiscovered Country became a real translation project.

hook: The green alien kept coming back pink.
fact: During an Orion makeup test, a color timer assumed the green tint was a film problem and corrected it. The deliberately green character looked human again.

hook: Lwaxana could argue with herself.
fact: Majel Barrett played Lwaxana Troi and voiced the Enterprise computer. In scenes where Lwaxana questions the computer, the actress effectively performs both sides of the conversation.

hook: The Romulan commander also became G’Kar.
fact: Andreas Katsulas returned as Tomalak while beginning his Babylon 5 run as G’Kar. He had also just played the one-armed man in The Fugitive.
